_about: Package VT, 2026-11-17: which of our own pictograms (design/twin-dial/vt/pictograms.js) the Twin Dial's check-control message draws, and the rule for anything we have no drawing for. Ids and meanings are package P's public-source catalogue (design/strip/pictograms/cc_catalogue.json, community numbering, UNVERIFIED on this car unless its 'g20' is true); this file only re-points the symbols to the larger Twin Dial set. The car's own symbol bitmaps (requestDefaultSymbols, symbol ids 0-6 seen so far) are maker's artwork: never drawn from, saved, baked, logged or committed.
_key: Symbols are chosen by the message's cCIdentifier (ccList entry id), not by its symbol id: the symbol id has no public enumeration and the car's log has not yet paired the two. Once the log shows (cCIdentifier, cCSymbolID) pairs, 'by_symbol_id' may be filled from that log (ids only, never the bitmaps).

generic_rule._why: Any id with no entry above (and every id while the table is unconfirmed on the car) gets a generic marker chosen by the message's colour (CCColorEnum), so a message is never drawn without a symbol and never with a wrong specific one.

fallback_window: A missing glyph in the message text (the message font lacks a character), no readable name, or a throw while drawing opens BMW's own panel (decision 6). A missing pictogram never does: the generic rule always yields one.
